Iran’s Three-Front Security State

Iran woke to a patrol ambush in Sistan and Baluchestan, two executions in Isfahan and a warning that Starlink could become a military target. The state faces gunmen on a southeastern highway, prisoners in its jails and satellite terminals on its rooftops.

Gunmen attacked a police patrol from the Nokju station near Bampur on the Bampur–Iranshahr road. Two officers, Amirhossein Ghasemi and Nezam Dastgoshadeh, were killed and a third was wounded, according to Iranian media. 

No group immediately claimed responsibility. Tasnim, a state-linked outlet, blamed forces it described as affiliated with the “U.S.-Israeli enemy.” 

Iran also executed Alireza Sepahi and Alireza Raeisi, two men arrested during the January protests in Isfahan. Iran’s judiciary said they were convicted of membership in an armed rebel group, “waging war against God” and involvement in the deaths of four police officers. 

Rights groups described them as protesters tried in the Alikhani Square case. The executions bring to at least seven the number of defendants in that case put to death, according to rights-monitoring reports. 

Mohammad Amin Aghamiri, secretary of Iran’s Supreme Council of Cyberspace, said the authorities had disabled Starlink terminals during the January unrest. 

He warned that satellite-internet infrastructure used for military purposes could become a target. Tehran treats internet access as a battlefield because a phone signal can mobilize a crowd faster than a police van can disperse it. 

Iranian Armed Forces Chief of Staff Maj. Gen. Ali Abdollahi gave the external version. A new war against Iran, he said, would spread across the region. 

If Washington moves against Tehran before or after the midterms, Iran would strike U.S. interests without limits. The message is aimed at Washington, but it lands on every Gulf state hosting American troops. 

Iran calls its enemies terrorists, rioters and foreign agents. The categories change according to the battlefield. The answer does not: treat every threat as war, then make the target disappear.

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Defense Ministry spokesperson Reza Talaei-Nik says any US or Israeli aggression against Iran would face a firm response, stressing the country’s readiness to counter threats.

Talaei-Nik told a press conference on Tuesday that resistance and national power were key to completing “the enemy’s defeat and safeguarding Iran’s rights”.
​
He also said domestic production of weapons and defense equipment had reached 2.5 times its level before the recent war, up from double the pre-war level announced three months earlier.
​
The increase was attributed to the capacity of knowledge-based companies and Iran’s defense industries, with production of some weapons rising more than threefold through private-sector participation.
​
Talaei-Nik warned that any renewed miscalculation by Iran’s adversaries would be met by more advanced weapons and equipment and a heavier response from the armed forces.
